ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows one large rectangle divided by one vertical line and one horizontal line into four smaller rectangles. The upper-left region is labeled 9 cm² and is the square described in the problem. The bottom-right region is shaded gray. The vertical cut forms the right edge of the upper-left square, and the horizontal cut forms its bottom edge. Reasoning: Since the upper-left square has area 9 cm², its side length is √9 = 3 cm. Let the whole rectangle have width W and height H. Its perimeter is 30 cm, so 2(W + H) = 30, hence W + H = 15. The shaded bottom-right rectangle has width W - 3 and height H - 3, because it excludes the 3 cm square strip dimensions from the left and top. Its perimeter is 2[(W - 3) + (H - 3)] = 2(W + H - 6) = 2(15 - 6) = 18 cm.

method.method_draft: Identify from the figure that the labeled upper-left region is the square mentioned in the text, with area 9 cm^2, so its side length is 3 cm. Let the whole rectangle have width W and height H. From the text, its perimeter is 30 cm, so 2(W+H)=30 and W+H=15. The shaded rectangle is the bottom-right region in the image; because the vertical and horizontal cuts lie along the right and bottom edges of the 3-by-3 square, its dimensions are W-3 and H-3. Therefore its perimeter is 2[(W-3)+(H-3)]=2(W+H-6)=2(15-6)=18 cm.

verify_reports.critic_suggestions: No revision needed. The reasoning trace accurately describes the image first, then reasons from the square area and whole-rectangle perimeter to obtain the shaded rectangle perimeter.

method.method_draft: Trace the shaded rectangle visually. Its perimeter consists of two equal pairs: the bottom shaded side equals the part of the whole rectangle's bottom edge to the right of the vertical cut, and the right shaded side equals the part of the whole rectangle's right edge below the horizontal cut. The upper-left square has area 9 cm^2, so each cut is 3 cm from the corresponding outer side. The sum of one full bottom side and one full right side of the outer rectangle is half the outer perimeter, 30/2=15 cm. To get the adjacent side-sum of the shaded rectangle, subtract the 3 cm left portion removed from the bottom direction and the 3 cm top portion removed from the height direction: 15-3-3=9 cm. Double this adjacent side-sum to get the shaded rectangle perimeter: 2*9=18 cm.
